title: Grateful Dead Live at Denver Coliseum on 1973-11-20

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a late‑1973 Denver show, highlighted by a smoking The Other One > Mind Left Body, China > Rider and an exceptional To Lay Me Down.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its crisp, well‑balanced mix – the instruments are clean and the piano sits forward while vocals sit a bit low. Musically the performance shines, with standout moments in The Other One > Mind Left Body, China > Rider, Tennessee Jed, Dire Wolf and an especially vivid To Lay Me Down. Minor quirks such as occasional stereo spread issues or a faint vocal level do not detract from what reviewers describe as one of the strongest late‑'73 shows.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 20 reviews, almost all 5‑star, consistently praise both performance and sound quality; only minor technical or mix complaints appear, supporting a top‑tier rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clean mix with all instruments well defined; piano is prominent, vocals are low but present. Some listeners note occasional stereo spread quirks and that the source is a 2‑track board feed rather than a true multitrack soundboard.

standout_songs: The Other One > Mind Left Body
show_quality.setlist_flow: Reviewers rave about seamless transitions, especially China into Rider and The Other One into Mind Left Body; the first set is described as “incredibly played,” while the second set contains several high‑water marks.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Generally praised for tone and guitar work; a few reviewers note he lagged a beat during the Mind Left Body jam, sparking debate about band dynamics.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass described as “bombs away,” clean and powerful throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Bob: His rhythm playing is highlighted as inventive, especially during The Other One jam.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's piano is noted for being clear and sitting forward in the mix, a rarity on many recordings.
